record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: For moduli spaces of supersymmetric gauge theories, Hilbert series (HS) and highest weight generating functions (HWGs) enumerate gauge-invariant operators, while phase diagrams encode the poset structure of symplectic leaves and transverse slices. Can one compute the phase diagrams directly from the corresponding HS or HWGs?

evidence.quote: Question 2. Can we compute the phase diagrams from the HS/HWGs?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a symplectic singularity, that is, a normal complex algebraic variety whose smooth locus carries a holomorphic symplectic 2-form that extends to a (possibly degenerate) regular 2-form on any resolution. Such an X admits a finite stratification into symplectic leaves; the closure-ordering on these leaves yields a finite graded poset (the Hasse / phase diagram), and to each covering relation L' < L one associates a transverse slice, itself a symplectic singularity, whose isomorphism type decorates the corresponding edge.

Suppose X is presented as the moduli space (Higgs or Coulomb branch) of a 3d N=4 quiver gauge theory, and that the following data are given:
(a) the Hilbert series HS_X(t,z) = Σ dim(R_n)_λ · t^n · z^λ, the refined generating function counting the graded multiplicities of the global-symmetry irreducible representations appearing in the coordinate ring R = C[X];
(b) the highest weight generating function HWG_X(μ,t), defined by HS_X(t,z) = Σ_{λ dominant} a_λ(t) · χ_λ(z), with HWG_X(μ,t) = Σ a_λ(t) μ^λ, encoding the same information by labeling representations through their highest weights.

Problem. Provide an algorithm that, taking only HS_X(t,z) and/or HWG_X(μ,t) as input, outputs the full phase diagram of X — namely the graded poset of symplectic leaf closures together with the transverse-slice decoration on every covering edge — and prove that the algorithm is correct. Equivalently: determine to what extent the data (HS_X, HWG_X) determine the Hasse diagram of symplectic leaves and its transverse-slice labels of X, and exhibit an explicit reconstruction procedure or an obstruction to one.
artifact.status_search_result: No general algorithm extracting Hasse/phase diagrams of symplectic leaves directly from Hilbert series or highest weight generating functions appears in the literature. Phase diagrams are typically computed via quiver subtraction or Kraft–Procesi transitions on the underlying quiver, not from HS/HWG data, and HS/HWG are usually treated as finer/separate invariants. Recent work (e.g. on classifying isolated symplectic singularities via 3d N=4 Coulomb branches) continues to treat the Hasse diagram, Hilbert series and HWG as independent ingredients in the characterization, suggesting the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Higgs mechanism — Hasse diagrams for symplectic singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Decomposition of Higgs branches into symplectic leaves with transverse slices, encoded in a Hasse diagram, is obtained via quiver subtraction on magnetic quivers.
status_evidence.claim: Hasse diagrams are computed via quiver subtraction, not directly from HS/HWG.

status_evidence.title: Lectures on Symplectic Singularities (Hanany, 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists invariants of symplectic singularities — dimension, global symmetry, Hasse diagram, Hilbert series, HWG, chiral ring — as separate items in increasing order of computational difficulty.
status_evidence.claim: HS, HWG and phase diagrams are listed as distinct invariants, with no algorithm given to derive the phase diagram from HS/HWG.

status_evidence.title: Classifying Isolated Symplectic Singularities via 3d N=4 Coulomb Branches
status_evidence.snippet: Recent classification work continues to combine HS, HWG, and Hasse diagrams as complementary characterizations.
status_evidence.claim: The reconstruction problem is still treated implicitly as open.
